Q2'26 Review: AWS Revenue Growth & Operating Margins Support the RoIC Behind AI Investments; Overall Profit Margin Multi-Year Thesis Building in Momentum
AMZN
12m Price Target: $375.00
Upside: 59.2%

AMZN's Q2'26 earnings report featured several key themes: 1) AWS's revenue growth rate (+37%), operating margin (+39%), and momentum in their chips and AI businesses (each with a $25b annual revenue run rate) continue to demonstrate a clear signal of return on invested capital as tailwinds build around the company's competitive positioning relative to the AI secular growth theme across compute workloads, custom silicon and increasingly enabling AI adoption through choice (with mgmt. estimating AWS could reach a $1tn annual run rate); 2) Capex (while increased from $200b to $220b for 2026 to reflect inflationary component pricing) continues to be framed by management as a signal of both strong visibility into the return profile and supportive of the company revenue backlog (now standing at $496b +154% YoY) which will likely remain supportive of continued AWS revenue growth acceleration in the coming quarters; 3) the overall health of the Amazon Prime consumer remains solid/strong and growing initiatives around a wider array of supply (especially groceries and household essentials) and geographies (+80 new cities this quarter alone), faster delivery times and continued adoption of Alexa for Shopping (+350m customers LTM) are supportive of the company's relative positioning to be one of the strongest secular growth themes in our coverage universe away from AI; & 4) advertising revenue growth (+26% YoY) continues to be supported by both the core eCommerce operations and a growing mix from Prime Video (particular engagement with live sports – i.e., NBA), programmatic advertising etc. In total, this earnings report was fully supportive of the company's operating momentum, its current pace/cadence of investments and the ability medium/long-term to produce sustained RoIC against those investments (across multiple areas of the business).

Over the short-term, we would expect investor debates will remain centered on the slope and scale of the overall AWS opportunity (primarily in the form of AI momentum but also by a wider array of operating elements of overall workload migration toward cloud

environment), profile and cadence of capex growth, the health of the global consumer landscape, the ability for AMZN to sustain Ad Services growth (even at more normalized levels as revenue growth comps become more difficult) & how any newer investment initiatives (AI, Project Leo, quick commerce, supply array and geographic expansion) might impact the linearity of operating profit growth. Over the next 12+ months, we reiterate our view that Amazon can produce a strong mix of compounded revenue growth and operating margin expansion on a multi-year horizon while continuing to make critical investments in long-term growth initiatives. We see AMZN as well positioned for future outperformance as: 1) AWS benefits from a long-tailed structural growth opportunity in the shifting needs of enterprise customers with tailwinds from the ramp of Gen AI workloads; 2) eCommerce margins continue to benefit from higher volumes across a more efficient logistics network and reductions in cost to serve per unit; & 3) the advertising business continues to scale at high margins against rising market opportunities in retail media, programmatic advertising and evolving media consumption habits. We reiterate our Buy rating and raise our 12-month PT from $335 to $375 as we adjust our forward operating estimates for this earnings report and updated management commentary. At the after-hours price of $258, AMZN is now trading at ~25x our 2027 GAAP EPS estimate when compared to 23% YoY growth in GAAP EPS over 2026. The company screens as one of the most compelling risk/rewards in our coverage universe.
Q2'26 Positives & Negatives:

Positives: a) Q2 consolidated revenue came in above the high-end of the guide & GSe/FactSet Street estimates at $200.6bn (+20% YoY) driven by strength in AWS (+37% YoY), Advertising (+26% YoY), North America, & Third Party Seller Services; b) Continued strength in the chips and AI businesses (each seeing triple digits YoY % growth rates and $25b annual runrates) with revenue commitments for Graviton increasing nearly 3x QoQ and management expressing the potential for AWS to become $1tn annual revenue business; c) 2Q AWS operating margins of +39% (above GSe/Street of ~34%) as incremental margins from additional AI and core workloads come in better than expected; & d) In retail, return on investments in quick commerce continues to materialize through traction with perishable offerings (monthly customers growing +50% since the start of the year), expansion in Amazon Now (added 80 new cities in 2Q), and Everyday Essentials growing meaningfully faster than other US categories.

Negatives: a) Q3'26 revenue and operating income guidance came below GSe/Street expectations by (3)%/(2)% and (9)%/(3)% respectively at the midpoint, though this includes ~80bps of headwind from FX and a 400bps impact from the Prime day timing shift; & b) Mgmt guided elevated FY26 capex to $220bn (vs $200bn previously guided) and noted heighten input costs (i.e., memory) as the main driver.
Q3'26 & 2026 Estimate Changes:

Q3'26: Revenue of $201.5bn (from $206.66bn prior); GAAP EBIT of $26.04bn (from $26.82bn prior); & GAAP EPS of $1.90 (from $1.96 prior). 2026: Revenue of $825.1bn (from $827.60bn prior); GAAP EBIT of $109.4bn (from $106.71bn prior); & GAAP EPS of $12.76 (from $8.85 prior).

GS Factor Profile

The GS Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks) and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:

Growth is based on a stock's forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock's forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock's forward-looking P/E, P/B, price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).

Financial Returns and Multiple use the GS analyst forecasts at the fiscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs for the fiscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics).
For a more detailed description of how we calculate the GS Factor Profile, please contact your GS representative.
M&A Rank

Across our global coverage, we examine stocks using an M&A framework, considering both qualitative factors and quantitative factors (which may vary across sectors and regions) to incorporate the potential that certain companies could be acquired. We then assign a M&A rank as a means of scoring companies under our rated coverage from 1 to 3, with 1 representing high (30%-50%) probability of the company becoming an acquisition target, 2 representing medium (15%-30%) probability and 3 representing low (0%-15%) probability. For companies ranked 1 or 2, in line with our standard departmental guidelines we incorporate an M&A component into our target price. M&A rank of 3 is considered immaterial and therefore does not factor into our price target, and may or may not be discussed in research.
